chunks: My father narrated to me from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from Muḥammad ibn Ūramah, from Zakariyyā al-Muʾmin Abū ʿAbdillāh, from ʿAbdillāh ibn Yaḥyā al-Kāhili, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever wishes to be among the honoured by Allāh on the Day of Resurrection and to be included in the intercession of Muḥammad (peace be upon him and his family), let him be a visitor of al-Ḥusayn. He will attain from Allāh bounty and honour, and good reward, and He will not question him about any sin he committed during his worldly life, even if his sins were as numerous as the grains of sand of ʿĀlij, the mountains of Ṭihāmah, and the foam of the sea. Verily, al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) was killed wrongfully and oppressed, his soul being thirsty, as were his family and his companions.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of visiting Imam al-Husayn according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the theological weight of Ziyārah as a conduit for divine favor, linking the visitor’s status directly to the intercession of the Prophet and the specific merit of Imām al-Ḥusayn’s unjust martyrdom. It highlights the Shia concept of *maghfirah* (forgiveness) not merely as a transactional absolution but as a profound spiritual elevation, where the intensity of his suffering—marked by thirst and oppression—serves as the catalyst for erasing even the multitude of one's sins. This narrative reinforces the centrality of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shia soteriology, positioning their suffering as a redemptive force for the faithful.
